rationale: I call Slide A as the MSI-H/dMMR tumour, on morphology. Slide A carries three of the features that are relatively specific for dMMR and concentrates them: intraepithelial lymphocytes within tumour epithelium at roughly 3-6 per 130 um field, a dense band-like and partly nodular peritumoral lymphoplasmacytic reaction at the invasive edge, and a medullary-like solid focus of syncytial cells with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli - set against marked intratumoural heterogeneity (cribriform, micropapillary and solid patterns in one slide). Slide B is the opposite: one monotonous well-differentiated villoglandular pattern across all six fields, with lymphocytes restricted to stromal cores and the tumour epithelium essentially free of IELs. The genuine counterweight is that Slide B's overview shows extracellular mucin lakes dissecting the wall with a pushing nodular outline, and mucinous differentiation is MSI-associated - but it is far less specific than TILs plus medullary growth (most mucinous colorectal carcinomas are still MSS), and Slide B lacks every other dMMR feature, so I weight A's lymphocytic and medullary findings higher. Against my own call, Slide A has a desmoplastic infiltrative border and cribriform glands with dirty luminal necrosis, both more typical of conventional MSS carcinoma, which is why my confidence is moderate rather than high. The two slides do differ noticeably in staining - A is magenta with strong eosin and a violet haematoxylin, B is a deeper blue-purple with crisper chromatin - consistent with different scanners and stain batches; I scored only architecture, cell-level features and lymphocyte position, and the colour difference did not enter the call.

Slide A is the MSI-H candidate on three concordant features: solid/medullary growth in syncytial sheets with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli and essentially no gland formation, a dense population of small round hyperchromatic intraepithelial lymphocytes within those sheets confirmed at 3x upscaling, and two morphologically distinct patterns in one slide (solid sheets plus single-cell infiltration through muscularis). Slide B is, in every tumour field sampled, a well-differentiated conventional adenocarcinoma of tall pseudostratified columnar glands with lymphocytes restricted to the stroma and almost none inside the epithelium. The countervailing evidence is B's apparent extracellular mucin pools around pushing glandular nests in the deep wall on the overview, plus a discrete lymphoid aggregate in B field 6; neither was corroborated at high power (none of B's six fields contained mucin lakes or signet-ring cells), and mucin and a single mural follicle are far less specific for dMMR than brisk tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes with medullary growth. The two slides do differ in staining - A is darker and more magenta with softer nuclear detail, B brighter and crisper, consistent with different scanners and stain batches - which I deliberately did not weigh; the lymphocytes in A were identified by size, roundness and absent cytoplasm, and B's epithelium remained lymphocyte-poor despite its superior nuclear detail. Against the call: A also shows an infiltrative rather than pushing front at the muscle, and its two stroma-only fields limited the tumour actually sampled, hence confidence in the upper 70s rather than higher.

Slide A combines all the classic dMMR features: syncytial solid/medullary sheets with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli, poor gland formation, numerous lymphocyte-sized hyperchromatic nuclei lying inside the tumour epithelium, and a confluent nodular lymphoid sheet at the deep aspect consistent with a Crohn-like reaction, plus a second infiltrative small-nest pattern in the same slide (heterogeneity). Slide B is the opposite phenotype: a uniformly well-formed villoglandular adenocarcinoma with tall pseudostratified goblet-cell-rich epithelium, lymphocytes restricted to stromal cores, and no solid, medullary, signet-ring or heterogeneous areas in any of the four informative tumour fields. The two slides differ markedly in colour balance - A is eosin-dominant pink/magenta, B is haematoxylin-dominant deep purple - which makes nuclei in B look darker and denser overall; I deliberately scored TILs by position relative to the epithelial basement membrane and by nuclear size at 450px zoom rather than by staining intensity, and the colour difference did not drive the call. The one feature pointing the other way is B's rounded, pushing invasive front on the overview with possible peritumoural mucin, but that is outweighed by the complete absence of intraepithelial lymphocytes and the well-differentiated gland formation in B. Call: A is the MSI-H / dMMR tumour, on morphology.

The two slides differ markedly in stain and focus - A is a flat, dull purple-magenta with weak eosin and slightly soft focus, B is crisp with vivid magenta nuclei and strong pink stroma - and I deliberately did not let that drive the call. On morphology, Slide A is a high-grade, poorly gland-forming carcinoma: cribriform and solid syncytial sheets with vesicular nuclei and nucleoli, three or more distinct patterns across six fields, and at high zoom a steady population of 5-7 um dark round lymphocytes sitting between tumour cells plus a dense lymphoplasmacytic band at the invasive front. Slide B, by contrast, is a uniform well-differentiated villiform adenocarcinoma whose epithelium is almost free of intraepithelial lymphocytes at identical magnification, with lymphocytes restricted to stromal cores and to a lymphoid follicle in non-neoplastic mucosa. The two features that weigh against A - its infiltrative desmoplastic border, and the fact that its brisk front-of-tumour inflammation co-localises with endoscopic tattoo pigment - are real, as is the pushing nodular, possibly mucinous invasive front seen on B's overview, and they are why I am not more confident. But intraepithelial lymphocyte density and loss of gland formation are the two strongest H&E discriminators for dMMR, and both point to A.

Slide A is a poorly differentiated, largely non-gland-forming carcinoma with one field of frankly solid, syncytial, medullary-like growth (vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli) and marked morphologic heterogeneity between fields, and it carries a heavy lymphocytic infiltrate in which small dark lymphocytes are clearly intraepithelial at high zoom. Slide B is uniformly well differentiated across every sampled field, with tall columnar pseudostratified epithelium and lymphocytes essentially restricted to the stroma; its only MSI-leaning features are a single large peritumoral lymphoid aggregate and possible mucin pools seen only on the overview. The TIL gradient (3 vs 1) plus poor differentiation, medullary-like solid growth and heterogeneity all point the same way, so I call A as the MSI-H/dMMR tumour. Two findings argue against that call and keep my confidence moderate: slide A has a distinctly infiltrative, single-cell invasive front into muscularis propria rather than the pushing border typical of dMMR, and it shows no mucinous or signet-ring differentiation at all. The two slides do differ in stain and colour balance - A is a duller pink-magenta with greyer nuclei, B a more saturated magenta-purple with crisp white lumina - and I deliberately did not let that difference contribute; the call rests on architecture and on lymphocyte position relative to tumour epithelium.

Slide A combines the three features that carry most weight for dMMR: a medullary-like solid/syncytial growth pattern with vesicular nuclei and prominent nucleoli and essentially no gland formation in 4 of 6 fields; intraepithelial lymphocytes clearly resolvable within the tumour sheets at 0.5 um/px; and a Crohn-like peritumoral reaction, including a germinal-centre-bearing lymphoid nodule in muscularis propria remote from the tumour, with a broad pushing deep border on the overview. It also shows two coexisting morphologies (solid and cribriform). Slide B is a monotonous, well-formed complex glandular adenocarcinoma with pseudostratified cigar-shaped nuclei, abundant apoptotic debris but scant true intraepithelial lymphocytes, and lymphoid tissue that abuts rather than infiltrates the epithelium - a conventional MSS-type phenotype. The one feature favouring B is probable extracellular mucin around the deep nests on its overview, but that is a lower-weight and, at 8 um/px, an unconfirmed finding, and it does not outweigh A's medullary growth plus lymphoid phenotype. The two slides do differ in stain and colour balance (A bluer/more magenta, B pinker with crisper nuclear detail); this was noted and deliberately excluded from the call, which rests on architecture, nuclear features and lymphocyte distribution alone.
